headline: FBI pins $6.3B Binance heist on North Korea as scammers circle users; Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days stay the top patch priority

bullets.text: New since the last SITREP: Help Net Security reports the FBI has pinned the $6.3 billion Binance heist on North Korea while scammers circle anxious users. Earlier reports name TraderTraitor and say the FBI flagged over 600 addresses.

Also new: BleepingComputer confirms Ivanti patched two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of today, 2026-11-02, and 2026-11-13.
Polymarket returned $3.9 million to traders, and DebugBear cites a DNS hijack, SecurityWeek reports. The Hacker News earlier described about $2.7 million stolen through a hijacked DebugBear script.
The Hacker News reports a new VOLTA infostealer that uses Claude, Gemini and Kimi AI to rank victims by financial value.
CISA KEV due dates for the max-severity GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229 and the Cisco ASA/FTD flaw CVE-2026-76418 passed on 2026-11-01. Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab after an attempted RCE attack.
The official Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace was trojanized with a persistent SSH backdoor; WIRED reports malicious Claude extensions reached thousands of devices.

actions: If you handle crypto transactions, screen against the addresses the FBI flagged for the Binance heist, and warn staff about Binance-themed scams.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches today, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
If GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) or Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) are still unpatched, patch now; both KEV due dates have passed.
Find any LXD and MicroCloud deployments, check the vendor advisory for the CVSS 10.0 flaw, and patch them.
If your sites load the DebugBear script, review it against DebugBear's DNS hijack statement and check for injected code.
If developers use the Claude Code extension in Cursor, check it against the vendor advisory and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.
